title: Dutch Oven Beef Stew with Olives and Corn
ingredients: 2 lbs beef stew meat (chuck roast, cut into 1.5-inch cubes)
3 medium Yukon Gold or Russet potatoes, cut into bite-sized chunks
1/2 cup green olives (pitted, whole or halved)
1 cup corn kernels (fresh, frozen, or canned)
1 tsp dried thyme or 2 sprigs fresh thyme
Salt and fresh cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Sear the beef: Pat the beef dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef in a single layer (work in batches if needed to avoid overcrowding) and sear until browned on all sides, about 6–8 minutes total. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

Sauté aromatics and create roux base: Turn heat down to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, then the diced onion. Cook for 4–5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir continuously for 1 minute to cook out the raw flour taste.

Deglaze and build the broth: Slowly pour in the beef broth, scraping up all the browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Stir in the soy sauce, thyme, bay leaf, and the seared beef along with any juices left on the plate. Bring to a simmer.
Braise low and slow: Cover the Dutch oven, reduce heat to low, and simmer gently for 1 hour.

Add potatoes, carrots, olives and corn: Uncover and stir in the potatoes, carrots, olives, and corn. Cover again and simmer for another 45–50 minutes, until the beef is melt-in-your-mouth tender and the potatoes and carrots are easily pierced with a fork.

Season and serve: Remove from heat and discard the bay leaf. Taste the broth and adjust salt and pepper if needed (soy sauce is salty, so you may need less added salt). Let sit for 5–10 minutes before serving so the stew thickens slightly.
notes: Serving size is about 1.5 cups (1 of 6 servings)
